title: The oven niche
body:
My Naomi. If you are reading this, you came home, and I am already Home. Don't cry on the dough — it makes it salty. I know what they said about you in Caesarea. I never believed a word. Fear will tell you to hide in this kitchen. Don't.
"There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear." (1 John 4:18)
Open the shutters.
— your Savta

title: Behind the loose brick
body:
Every morning for fifty years I lit that oven in the dark, not knowing if anyone would buy a single loaf. Someone always came.
"It is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness." (Lamentations 3:22–23)
The well remembers everything, little one. Go and listen.
— your Savta

title: Under the bucket stone
body:
Half this town has decided a man is guilty before breakfast. I have done it too, God forgive me.
"He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him." (Proverbs 18:13)
Hear the whole matter, Naomi. Especially from the ones who aren't talking.
— your Savta

title: In the well's foundation
body:
I carved this one for the well because it is the loudest place in Joppa.
"A froward man soweth strife: and a whisperer separateth chief friends." (Proverbs 16:28)
A rumor is a crack in a jar. It doesn't break all at once. It just leaks until nothing is left. Mend what you can.
— your Savta

title: In Savta's shard basket
body:
Marcus. I wrote you every month. You never answered, and I never stopped. When you come back — and you will — know this:
"But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him." (Luke 15:20)
Nobody has to earn their way back to this table.
— your Savta

title: In Silas's net box
body:
For both my grandchildren, who are stubborn like their grandfather. When the whole harbor is against you, remember who stands with you.
"The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my strength, in whom I will trust; my buckler, and the horn of my salvation, and my high tower." (Psalm 18:2)
— your Savta

title: In Tabitha's sewing basket
body:
Tabitha and I made a pact: whoever went first would leave something for the other's girl. If you are reading this, she found you. Grief is not a lack of faith, Naomi.
"Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning." (Psalm 30:5)
Wait for the morning.
— your Savta

title: Under Simon the tanner's doorstep
body:
People hold their noses at this house. Holy things happen in the places people hold their noses at. The Lord came
"to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness." (Isaiah 61:3)
Tabitha sewed that verse into everything she ever made.
— your Savta
